claims.statement: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) is a crucial interface that separates the vascular system from the central nervous system (CNS).

evidence_spans.raw_text: The three primary barriers or interfaces that separate the vascular system from the CNS are strictly controlled. These three barriers include i) the arachnoid barrier, ii) the blood–cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB), and iii) the BBB itself.
evidence_spans.quote: The three primary barriers or interfaces that separate the vascular system from the CNS are strictly controlled.
evidence_spans.rationale: The sentence supports the claim by mentioning the BBB as one of the three primary barriers that separate the vascular system from the CNS.

claims.statement: The BBB is formed by brain microvessel endothelial cells (BMECs), which separate the blood in the capillaries from the interstitial fluid (ISF) in the brain compartment.

evidence_spans.raw_text: The BBB is formed by brain microvessel endothelial cells (BMECs, also known as BMVECs and BECs), which separate the blood in the capillaries from the interstitial fluid (ISF) in the brain compartment.
evidence_spans.quote: The BBB is formed by brain microvessel endothelial cells (BMECs, also known as BMVECs and BECs), which separate the blood in the capillaries from the interstitial fluid (ISF) in the brain compartment.
evidence_spans.rationale: The sentence supports the claim by describing the formation of the BBB by BMECs.
